record.original_question: How should alternating virtual knots be defined and classified, what is the correct analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture in the virtual setting, and how can one classify alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization?

evidence.quote: Define and classify alternating virtual knots. Find an analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture and prove it. Compare [110] Classify all alternating weaves on surfaces (without stabilization).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A virtual knot is an equivalence class of knot diagrams in the plane with classical and virtual crossings, taken modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves; equivalently, a virtual knot is an equivalence class of knots in thickened orientable surfaces under ambient isotopy, orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the surface, and stabilization/destabilization (addition/removal of handles disjoint from the knot). A diagram is called alternating if, traversing the knot, classical crossings alternate between over and under (virtual crossings are ignored for this purpose). A flype is the local move on a tangle T inside a diagram that takes a 2-strand configuration with a single crossing adjacent to T and rotates T by 180°, moving the crossing to the opposite side.

(a) Give an intrinsic definition of "alternating virtual knot" and produce a classification of alternating virtual knots.

(b) Formulate and prove an analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture in the virtual setting: namely, identify the precise class of reduced alternating diagrams representing a given alternating virtual knot and show that any two such diagrams are related by a finite sequence of flypes (together with any additional moves needed in the virtual category).

(c) Classify all alternating weaves on closed orientable surfaces without allowing stabilization, where a weave on a surface Σ is a 4-valent graph on Σ together with over/under information at each vertex, considered up to ambient isotopy and Reidemeister moves on Σ.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. Boden–Karimi–Sikora established Tait's first and second conjectures for alternating links in thickened surfaces and for virtual links, and Karimi's 2018 PhD thesis "Alternating Virtual Knots" gives an intrinsic definition and partial classification. Kindred's 2022 "Virtual flyping theorem" (arXiv:2210.03720) proves that any two locally prime, cellular alternating diagrams of a link in a thickened surface are related by flypes, supplying the virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture. The full classification of alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization does not appear to be completely resolved.

status_evidence.title: The virtual flyping theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Any two locally prime, cellular alternating diagrams of a link in a thickened surface are related by flypes; all locally prime alternating diagrams of a virtual link have the same crossing number and writhe.
status_evidence.claim: Virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture is proved for alternating links in thickened surfaces.

status_evidence.title: Alternating Virtual Knots (Karimi PhD thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: PhD thesis defining alternating virtual knots and proving Tait-type results.
status_evidence.claim: Definition and partial classification of alternating virtual knots given.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of alternating links in thickened surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Boden–Karimi–Sikora characterize alternating links in thickened surfaces and prove the first two Tait conjectures in this setting.
status_evidence.claim: First two Tait conjectures established for alternating virtual/thickened-surface links.
